ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AD$ and $AE$ are the median and altitude on side $BC$, respectively. If $\angle B=40^\circ$ and $\angle C=50^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle DAE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle B=40^\circ$ and $\angle C=50^\circ$, \\
therefore, $\angle BAC=90^\circ$, \\
and since AD is the median, \\
thus AD$= \frac{1}{2}$ BC$=$BD, \\
hence, $\angle ADE=2\angle B=80^\circ$, \\
and since AE$\perp$BC, \\
therefore, $\angle DAE=\boxed{10^\circ}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle B=40^\circ$ and $\angle C=50^\circ$, \\ therefore, $\angle BAC=90^\circ$, \\ and since AD is the median, \\ thus AD$= \frac{1}{2}$ BC$=$BD, \\ hence, $\angle ADE=2\angle B=80^\circ$, \\ and since AE$\perp$BC, \\ therefore, $\angle DAE=\boxed{10^\circ}$
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
First describe the image: In the figure is triangle ABC, A is above, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, and BC is a horizontal base. D and E are both on BC, and D is to the left of E. Line segment AD connects from A to D, and line segment AE goes from A perpendicular to the base BC. There is a right-angle mark at E in the figure, indicating AE⊥BC.

Then reason: It is known that ∠B=40° and ∠C=50°, so ∠BAC=180°-40°-50°=90°. Therefore △ABC is a right triangle with A as the right angle, and BC is the hypotenuse. AD is the median on hypotenuse BC, so AD=BD=CD. Thus in △ABD, AD=BD, so ∠BAD=∠ABD. Because D is on BC, ∠ABD=∠ABC=40°, therefore ∠BAD=40°. Also because AE⊥BC, in △ABE, ∠BAE=90°-∠B=90°-40°=50°. In the figure AD is between AB and AE, so ∠DAE=∠BAE-∠BAD=50°-40°=10°.

Final answer: 10°
